Two lines saved XOR. Is the last layer enough?

KP02 left two questions: what do more lines cut, and can the last layer still separate any labelling?

Bit: a point on the positive side of a line (score >0>0>0) gets 1, otherwise 0.

Step rule: a positive score gives 1, otherwise 0.

Today: what do three lines cut, and what can the last layer (the output layer) do?

Three lines cut seven cells, each with a code

A point on the positive side of a line gets one bit. So what does the plane look like when three lines cut it together?

Code: the three bits y1y2y3y_1y_2y_3y1​y2​y3​ of a point, written in a row like a house number.

Cell: all points that share one code form one piece of the plane.

Take the point (1,1): the scores g1=x1, g2=x2, g3=−x1+x2−1g_1=x_1,\ g_2=x_2,\ g_3=-x_1+x_2-1g1​=x1​, g2​=x2​, g3​=−x1​+x2​−1 are 1, 1, −11,\ 1,\ -11, 1, −1, so the bits are 1, 1, 01,\ 1,\ 01, 1, 0 and the code is 110.

Three bits allow 8 codes, but the plane shows only 7 cells: which one is missing?

No point gets 101: its conditions contradict

Three bits allow eight codes, yet the plane shows only seven cells. Why can no point receive 101?

① Bit 1 is 1: we need x1>0x_1>0x1​>0 (right of the vertical line).

② Bit 2 is 0: we need x2≤0x_2\leq0x2​≤0 (on or below the horizontal line).

③ Bit 3 is 1: we need x2>x1+1x_2>x_1+1x2​>x1​+1 (above the slanted line), but ① and ② already force x2≤0<x1+1x_2\leq0<x_1+1x2​≤0<x1​+1.

The three regions share no point: 101 is an unrealized code, writable but received by no input. The other seven are realized codes.

Read codes as cube corners; the output is one cut

Only seven codes are realized and 101 is not. So what does the last layer do with these codes?

Vertex: a corner of the cube. A 3-bit code gives its coordinates (y1,y2,y3)(y_1,y_2,y_3)(y1​,y2​,y3​); there are 8 of them.

Output score: q=a1y1+a2y2+a3y3+a0q=a_1y_1+a_2y_2+a_3y_3+a_0q=a1​y1​+a2​y2​+a3​y3​+a0​. q>0q>0q>0 means class A, otherwise class B (A and B are the two class labels).

The output layer is the plane q=0q=0q=0 (an example in the figure): one cut that splits the corners into two sides.

Score each corner: 3 A's positive, 4 B's not

The output plane scores every corner with qqq. With q=−y1−y2+y3+0.5q=-y_1-y_2+y_3+0.5q=−y1​−y2​+y3​+0.5, are the seven realized corners separated?

Class A (blue, q>0q>0q>0)
000: −0−0+0+0.5=0.5-0-0+0+0.5=0.5−0−0+0+0.5=0.5
001: −0−0+1+0.5=1.5-0-0+1+0.5=1.5−0−0+1+0.5=1.5
011: −0−1+1+0.5=0.5-0-1+1+0.5=0.5−0−1+1+0.5=0.5

Class B (orange, q≤0q\leq0q≤0)
010: −0−1+0+0.5=−0.5-0-1+0+0.5=-0.5−0−1+0+0.5=−0.5
100: −1−0+0+0.5=−0.5-1-0+0+0.5=-0.5−1−0+0+0.5=−0.5
110: −1−1+0+0.5=−1.5-1-1+0+0.5=-1.5−1−1+0+0.5=−1.5
111: −1−1+1+0.5=−0.5-1-1+1+0.5=-0.5−1−1+1+0.5=−0.5

Linearly separable: one plane puts all of A on one side and all of B on the other.

Back in the plane, region A has a notch

By the corner scores, one plane puts all of A on one side and all of B on the other. Back in the input plane, what does region A look like?

Convex: for any two points of the region, the segment between them stays inside.

Union: several cells merged into one region.

P(−0.15,−1)P(-0.15,-1)P(−0.15,−1) and Q(−0.15,2)Q(-0.15,2)Q(−0.15,2) both lie in region A, yet segment PQPQPQ passes through the B cell at RRR: region A is not convex. But can any cells be merged?

A second labelling: XOR returns on the bottom face

Region A can be several cells joined. Can any cells be joined? Try A = {000, 110, 111}.

Look at the bottom face y3=0y_3=0y3​=0 only: its four corners are realized codes, with A on one diagonal and B on the other, just like the XOR of KP01. This labelling is nonseparable: it is a counterexample.

The diagonals share a midpoint: a contradiction

The bottom face alternates A and B. Since y3=0y_3=0y3​=0, a3a_3a3​ plays no role: can any a0,a1,a2a_0,a_1,a_2a0​,a1​,a2​ separate them?

① Add the A corners: q(000)+q(110)=a0+(a1+a2+a0)q(000)+q(110)=a_0+(a_1+a_2+a_0)q(000)+q(110)=a0​+(a1​+a2​+a0​)
=a1+a2+2a0>0=a_1+a_2+2a_0>0=a1​+a2​+2a0​>0
Two positive scores add up to a positive sum.

② Add the B corners: q(010)+q(100)=(a2+a0)+(a1+a0)q(010)+q(100)=(a_2+a_0)+(a_1+a_0)q(010)+q(100)=(a2​+a0​)+(a1​+a0​)
=a1+a2+2a0≤0=a_1+a_2+2a_0\leq0=a1​+a2​+2a0​≤0
Two nonpositive scores add up to a nonpositive sum.

③ Contradiction: one sum cannot be both >0>0>0 and ≤0\leq0≤0. Since qqq is linear, the score at the midpoint MMM is the average of both pairs, so the two demands conflict.

Not hopeless: one cut is not enough, add a layer

One sum had to be both >0>0>0 and ≤0\leq0≤0. Is a single output plane hopeless, or can it be repaired?

Answer to page 1: one output plane cannot separate every labelling (a two-layer network is a row of lines plus one output plane).

But it can be repaired: any single corner can be cut off. Cut 000, 110 and 111 one by one (right figure) and merge the results to get A.

Next KP: how can one more layer pick out chosen corners?

Extension: practice with a3 and the label 101

Can changing a coefficient, or relabeling 101, get around the limit of these lines plus one plane?

Question 1: does labeling the unrealized code 101 as A or B change any prediction?

Question 2: with A = {000, 110, 111}, can changing only a3a_3a3​ remove the contradiction?

Hint 1: does any input receive code 101?

Hint 2: all four bottom-face points have y3=0y_3=0y3​=0.

Worked solution (Question 2): ① Both sums equal a1+a2+2a0a_1+a_2+2a_0a1​+a2​+2a0​. ② With y3=0y_3=0y3​=0, the term a3⋅0a_3\cdot0a3​⋅0 vanishes. ③ So both sums are independent of a3a_3a3​ and the contradiction remains. ④ Check: for a3=100a_3=100a3​=100 both sums are unchanged.

Extension: p lines and d-dimensional inputs

Changing only a3 did not remove the contradiction, and relabeling 101 changed nothing. How is the code written for p lines and d dimensions?

gi(x)=wiTx+bi,y=[f(g1(x)),…,f(gp(x))]T∈{0,1}pg_i(\mathbf x)=\mathbf w_i^T\mathbf x+b_i,\quad \mathbf y=[f(g_1(\mathbf x)),\ldots,f(g_p(\mathbf x))]^T\in\{0,1\}^pgi​(x)=wiT​x+bi​,y=[f(g1​(x)),…,f(gp​(x))]T∈{0,1}p
x\mathbf xx has ddd coordinates; wi\mathbf w_iwi​ is the coefficient vector and bib_ibi​ the constant of line iii; fff is the step rule. Each of the ppp lines gives one bit, so a code is a corner of the unit hypercube.

Hypercube: a cube in ppp dimensions; its corners are the 2p2^p2p codes.
